sum: A two-week camping route up the Myagdi Khola to Dhaulagiri Base Camp, then over French Pass and Dhampus Pass to Marpha, with glacier travel and three nights above 4,700 m. Not a teahouse trek.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route the rule is beside the point: without a full camping crew and a guide who knows the glacier, the timing of the rockfall above Italian Base Camp and the line across the Dhampus traverse in cloud, you should not be here.

access: Drive from Pokhara to Beni and on up the Myagdi Khola to Darbang, five to six hours in all. A rough track continues towards Takam and Muri, and some crews start walking higher up when it is open. The trek ends at Marpha or Jomsom, with a morning flight or a day's drive back to Pokhara.

photo.a: A small group of trekkers crosses a wide, snow-covered valley floor, with cloud streaming around the icy peak of Sita Chuchura behind.
photo.c: Hidden Valley behind Dhaulagiri, with Sita Chuchura

includes: tents, kitchen crew and all meals on the camping stages (full camping packages)
lodge beds and meals lower down
road transport from Pokhara and back

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, and a flight or jeep seat from Jomsom to Pokhara at the end
transportExtra: the bus or jeep from Pokhara to Darbang at the start
tips: Choose the agency for its record on this route: ask when their guide last crossed both passes and what rescue and communication equipment the crew carries.
Bring crampons or solid microspikes, a four-season sleeping bag rated to minus 20 °C and a down jacket, plus an ice axe if you know how to use one.
Check that your insurance covers helicopter evacuation up to 6,000 m, and that the porters are insured and equipped for snow.
Build in at least two spare days for weather. Tight schedules push groups over the passes in conditions they should wait out.
There is no phone signal for most of the route beyond Muri; a satellite phone or messenger is the only link.

days.t: Drive to Darbang, walk to Dharapani
days.note: Leave Pokhara early for the five to six hour drive via Beni. From Darbang, cross the Myagdi Khola on a suspension bridge and climb about 350 m through terraces to the ridge-top village of Dharapani, where Dhaulagiri and Gurja Himal first appear. Hot and steep in the afternoon.

A traversing day high above the river through the villages of Takam and Sibang, on a mix of old stone trail and newer jeep track. Descend to cross a side stream, then climb to the big Magar village of Muri. The Dhaulagiri range and Gurja Himal are in view for much of the day.

Drop steeply to the river, climb over a ridge with a view up the valley, then follow the west bank of the Myagdi Khola through Naura. The last stretch crosses steep grass slopes and rock steps on a narrow path. In rain it is slippery; take it slowly and keep a hand free.

The last houses are behind you. The trail climbs and falls through thick forest of bamboo, oak and rhododendron, crossing side streams on log bridges and passing a few herders' clearings, to the campsite at Dobang. Leeches are bad here in the wet months.

Cross the Myagdi Khola and climb through forest that thins from bamboo to pine and birch, with Dhaulagiri's west wall beginning to fill the sky ahead. A half day on purpose: you gain almost 600 m and tomorrow you go higher again.

Leave the trees behind and climb the lateral moraine to a grassy shelf beneath the west face of Dhaulagiri, which rises more than 4,000 m above camp. Arrive by lunch, rest, and listen for the avalanches that come off the face through the afternoon.

days.t: Acclimatization day at Italian Base Camp
days.note: Walk a few hundred metres up the moraine or the hillside behind camp and come back down for lunch. The crew uses the day to check ropes, crampons and loads, and the guide looks at the state of the rockfall gully and the glacier you cross tomorrow.

days.t: Italian Base Camp to Glacier Camp
days.note: The most dangerous hours of the trek. Start at first light, descend a loose moraine wall, sometimes on a fixed rope, and cross the glacier snout below slopes that shed rocks once the sun hits them. Then follow the rubble-covered ice up a narrow gorge to a tent site levelled on the glacier.

days.t: Glacier Camp to Dhaulagiri Base Camp
days.note: A slow morning on shifting moraine as the glacier bends east and the valley opens. Base camp sits on the ice below the north face, with Tukuche Peak and the icefall to the north-east col across the glacier. You are 530 m higher than last night, and headaches are common.

days.t: Acclimatization day at Dhaulagiri Base Camp
days.note: A second night at the same height before the passes. Walk a little way up the moraine towards French Pass, drink plenty and rest. Anyone whose symptoms are not clearly improving should go back down to Italian Base Camp with a guide today, not tomorrow.

days.t: Over French Pass to Hidden Valley
days.note: Climb the lateral moraine beside the upper glacier, then steeper snow or scree to the cairns on French Pass, three to four hours from camp. Tukuche Peak, Sita Chuchura and Dhaulagiri's north face stand all round. An easy descent leads into Hidden Valley and the coldest camp of the trip.

days.t: Over Dhampus Pass to Yak Kharka
days.note: A gentle two to three hour climb to Dhampus Pass, then a long, tiring traverse above 5,000 m across snow slopes and spurs before the trail finally drops towards the Kali Gandaki. In cloud the line is hard to find, and after fresh snow the slopes can avalanche. Camp is more than 1,500 m below the pass.

days.t: Yak Kharka to Jomsom via Marpha
days.note: A steep, knee-testing descent of 1,000 m on zigzags to the flagstone lanes and apple orchards of Marpha, then an hour and a half up the valley road to Jomsom with the afternoon wind at your back. Many crews end the walk at Marpha and drive the last stretch.

days.t: Fly or drive from Jomsom to Pokhara
days.note: Morning flight to Pokhara when the weather allows. If flights are cancelled, jeeps and buses run down the Kali Gandaki road through Tatopani and Beni and take most of the day.
